candidates.evidence: Single symmetric Lorentzian 2D at 2699.0 cm-1 with FWHM 32.1 cm-1 (residual at noise level; a second 2D component is not significant); I2D/IG = 3.0 (peak height); G at 1581.2 cm-1 with FWHM 14.2 cm-1; sp2 D band at 1348 cm-1 with I_D/I_G = 0.16; no other peaks in 1100-3000 cm-1 above noise.

Would need a multi-component 2D (about four components) with FWHM of roughly 50 cm-1 or more and I2D/IG below about 2. The measured 2D is one narrow component with I2D/IG about 3, so this is disfavoured.
Would give a broader, asymmetric 2D and a weaker I2D/IG than measured; no such asymmetry or intensity pattern is present.

hint_reasoning: material_hint is null, so there is no stated material to test. Identification is from peak positions, widths and intensity ratios. G near 1581 cm-1 and a single Lorentzian 2D near 2699 cm-1 at 532 nm, with I2D/IG about 3, match monolayer graphene on SiO2. The spectrum window (1100-3000 cm-1) does not cover the low-frequency region, so the substrate check and any other van der Waals material check are limited to these graphene-specific features.

peaks.assignment: D band (defect-activated breathing mode, zone-edge phonon near K)
peaks.source: Fit amplitude 832 +/- 45 counts. Assignment from Ferrari & Robertson, PRB 61, 14095 (2000) and Cancado et al., Nano Lett. 11, 3190 (2011). FWHM is 12.6 with a quartic baseline and 14-20 with lower-order baselines. Not angle-resolved, so pattern is null.

peaks.assignment: G band (in-plane sp2 E2g phonon at Gamma)
peaks.source: Fit amplitude 5331 +/- 42 counts. Assignment from Ferrari et al., PRL 97, 187401 (2006).

peaks.assignment: D' band (defect-activated, intravalley TO phonon near K) - TENTATIVE
peaks.source: Amplitude 40-85 counts with uncertainty about +/-25 across baseline choices, about 1.5-4 sigma, with width and centre on fit bounds. Treated as a weak shoulder on G, not a firm detection. Assignment from Cancado et al., Nano Lett. 11, 3190 (2011) and Eckmann et al., Nano Lett. 12, 3925 (2012).
Fit amplitude 16074 +/- 28 counts; single Lorentzian, residual at noise level. Assignment from Ferrari et al., PRL 97, 187401 (2006).

properties.name: layers
properties.source: Single symmetric 2D Lorentzian with FWHM 32 cm-1 and I2D/IG (height ratio) about 3.0, which is the monolayer signature (Ferrari et al., PRL 97, 187401, 2006). No multi-component 2D needed; bilayer rejected.

properties.name: defect_level
properties.source: I_D/I_G = 0.156 (range 0.148-0.166 across baseline choices), giving L_D about 11 nm; low-defect regime (Cancado et al., Nano Lett. 11, 3190, 2011).

properties.name: L_D_nm
properties.source: Cancado et al., Nano Lett. 11, 3190 (2011): L_D^2 = 2.4e-10 * lambda^4 / (I_D/I_G), lambda = 532 nm. Gives 10.8-11.4 nm across baseline choices; about +/-1 nm plus the formula's own calibration uncertainty. Treat as order of magnitude because it sits near the formula's lower validity bound (about 10 nm).

properties.name: defect_type
properties.value: point-like (vacancy or sp3/adsorbate) favoured over grain boundaries; vacancy vs sp3 not resolved
properties.source: I_D/I_D' is about 8-13 (1-sigma range) if D' is taken as measured, or lower-limit above about 9 at 2 sigma. Eckmann et al., Nano Lett. 12, 3925 (2012) give about 7 for vacancies, about 13 for sp3-type, and about 3.5 for boundaries. Weak D' rules out boundary-dominated disorder.

properties.name: doping_type
properties.source: G at 1581.2 cm-1 and FWHM 14 cm-1 are close to neutral monolayer values and suggest low doping. No calibrated G/2D correlation was performed, so this is not quantified (Pisana et al., Nat. Mater. 6, 198, 2007, for G vs doping).

properties.name: strain_sign
properties.source: Requires reference 2D/G position correlation to separate strain from doping. The position ratio 2D/G = 1.707 is not used for a strain call here.

citations: Ferrari AC, Meyer JC, Scardaci V, et al. Raman spectrum of graphene and graphene layers. PRL 97, 187401 (2006).
Ferrari AC, Robertson J. Interpretation of Raman spectra of disordered and amorphous carbon. PRB 61, 14095 (2000).
Cancado LG, Jorio A, Ferreira EHM, et al. Quantifying defects in graphene via Raman spectroscopy at different excitation energies. Nano Lett. 11, 3190 (2011).
Eckmann A, Felten A, Mishchenko A, et al. Probing the nature of defects in graphene by Raman spectroscopy. Nano Lett. 12, 3925 (2012).
Pisana S, Lazzeri M, Casiraghi C, et al. Breakdown of the adiabatic Born-Oppenheimer approximation in graphene. Nat. Mater. 6, 198 (2007).
limits: Window is 1100-3000 cm-1 only. Low-frequency modes (RBM, LA/TA region) and the Si substrate line at 520.7 cm-1 are outside the window, so the substrate and any low-frequency signatures were not checked. The identification rests on the G/2D pattern, which is specific to sp2 carbon but would not exclude other sp2 or carbon-based materials with peaks outside the window.
Single spot, no polarization series, no mapping. Edge-type and point-type defects cannot be separated, and the laser may sample a locally defected region that is not representative of the flake.

L_D = 11 nm uses the Cancado (2011) relation, which is calibrated for point-defect-dominated samples at specific excitation wavelengths. The value sits near the formula's lower validity bound (about 10 nm), so treat it as an order-of-magnitude estimate. It is not a measured density.

A broad background of roughly 2000-2700 counts spans 1100-1700 cm-1, falling to about 1200 at 2900 cm-1. Its origin cannot be determined from this spectrum (fluorescence, resist residue, or substrate). Baseline choice changes the D height by under about 5% but changes the D FWHM between 13 and 20 cm-1 and the D' amplitude between 40 and 115 counts.

D' is not firmly resolved: its amplitude is 1.5-4 sigma depending on baseline, and its width and centre sit on fit bounds. D+D' near 2930 cm-1 is not detected (fit amplitude 19 +/- 29 counts). The defect-type call (vacancy vs sp3) is therefore unresolved; grain boundaries are disfavoured.

Doping and strain are not quantified. No calibrated G/2D correlation was applied. G at 1581.2 cm-1 and 2D at 2699 cm-1 are consistent with low doping and little strain, but a reference or multi-laser data would be needed for a number.

The monolayer call relies on line shape and intensity ratio from a single spectrum. A 2D FWHM of 32 cm-1 is slightly broader than typical ideal values (about 24-28 cm-1), which may reflect disorder, strain or doping inhomogeneity within the spot. A small bilayer or multilayer region inside the laser spot cannot be excluded.

Noise is about 90 counts (1 sigma). Features below about 3 sigma (roughly 270 counts) are not claimed. No cosmic-ray spikes or residual outliers above 4 sigma were found (residual std 91 counts, equal to noise), so the artifacts list is empty.
Measurement temperature 295 K and laser 532 nm were taken as given. No temperature correction was applied; none is expected to matter at this precision.
